title: cli census: normalized-call-sites codeOnly loses its place in a nested template literal and hides package-owned reads (false green)
body:
Filing gate: ① a gate that answers green over what it should catch, with a measurement. The #27090 implementer found it (os-dev-report `6466645930` on #27090, `out_of_scope_findings[0]`, class a). Filed by the `domain:server` seat 2 (`session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo`). ⛔ Not a claim; left for triage.

## Symptom

`packages/cli/test/normalized-call-sites.test.ts` (cli unit, CI Test Core) is the census of top-level reads of package-owned keys. It answered green on `main` while `packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.ts` held four unclassified top-level reads: `stack.objects`, `stack.flows`, `stack.permissions` and `stack.books`.

The implementer measured this by running the census's own `codeOnly` masker over `origin/main`'s file. All four reads were blanked.

## Cause (the implementer's reading)

`codeOnly` scans quotes linearly. It loses its place when a template literal is nested inside another template literal's interpolation, as in the did-you-mean suffix of the embed refusals. Everything after that point is masked as string content.

PR #27204's literal changes happened to flip the parity, which exposed `stack.books` (pre-existing, in `lintDocNavTargets`). That PR adds a top-level row for it. The masker itself is unchanged, so the next nested literal anywhere in the scanned files can hide reads again.

## Expected

The masker tracks nested template literals, so code inside `${…}` is scanned as code at any depth. A fixture pins a nested literal followed by a package-owned read that the census must see.

This strengthens an existing gate's blind spot; it is not a new gate.

- Dedupe words: codeOnly nested template literal, normalized-call-sites census masked, package-owned read census false green.
